To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) we present a novel method for modelling articulated motion, 2) the method is based on clustering the body pose into regions that exhibit similar dynamical characteristics.

we present a novel approach for modelling human motion, which uses statistical techniques to automatically capture the characteristic motion dynamics in different regions of the pose space, which are then used to model the dynamics of different motion segments.

we have developed a new approach to modeling human motion that is based on clustering the body pose state space into connected regions that exhibit similar dynamical characteristics; that we have developed an efficient algorithm to automatically cluster these regions and model the dynamics in each of the regions using a Gaussian autoregreesive model; that our method can be used to recognize and track human activities that would require a large number of exemplars in an example based method; that our method is useful in tracking complicated motions such as turns
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a statistical model of the human motion that captures the non-linear and non-stationary characteristics of human motion, which are crucial to the success of any tracking or recognition algorithm.
developing statistical methods for modelling and analysing human motion. The work is motivated by the need for more robust methods for tracking articulated motion in video.
the development of a novel approach to tracking human motion using statistical models, which are able to capture the non-linear and non-stationary dynamics of typical human activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a very good and efficient way to represent and track articulated motion.
the method is a novel, robust, and computationally efficient approach to tracking articulated motion.
our method is able to capture the dynamics of articulated human motion, using a relatively small number of exemplars, and is able to track complicated activities like turns without key frames.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel method to model the dynamics of human motion.
the method is able to model the dynamics of the motion in a compact way and is able to track articulated motion with good results.
we have developed a new method to track human motion in a way that is more general than existing methods, and is more flexible in its ability to handle different activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to capture the complex dynamics of articulated human motion using statistical methods, without the need for 3D information, key frames or other special cases.

a small number of models can be used to capture the dynamics of complex human motions, and that the models themselves can be learned from a single training example, without the need for large training sets.
the human motion space is highly structured and that this can be exploited to model the dynamics of human motion in a compact way.
